audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 read Skill against whys[0] ('Level 1 favours you'), and 2+ items read Skill against whys[6] and late, which both say Tahm Kench takes over.
audit.why: packet.levelChart gives Volibear rows 0-5 and Tahm Kench row 6, matching the prose and the 51.56% figure.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 6 flipped in both layers with ratings adjusted.

audit.whatIsWrong: No stage carried a cooldown — packet.defects flags zero sequencing cues in the whole matchup.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive at 21/20/19/18/17s is the longest cooldown in his kit and his only disengage; that is the window the entire lane is played around.
audit.corrected: 21s written into the cooldown breakdown, dosFull[0] and spikes[0], with Tongue Lash's 7s rank-1 poke alongside it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Devour was called 'W Devour' and treated as his engage dive in six places, and 'R Abyssal Voyage' was named as his ultimate in three more. His stun was written as a plain Q.
audit.why: Devour is his R. Abyssal Voyage no longer exists — his W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s. And Tongue Lash only stuns when the target already carries three An Acquired Taste stacks, which any of his damage applies; otherwise it just slows and heals him. So the thing to track is your own stack count, not a cooldown. Thick Skin is a 3s cooldown that converts stored damage into a shield and heals him out of combat, which is why the Grievous Wounds buy matters more than waiting it out.
audit.corrected: Slots corrected, Abyssal Voyage removed, the three-stack stun condition and Thick Skin's real behaviour stated.

edits.before: - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: matchup-defining — His escape + shield. All-in when down. Track it before every engage. - Tahm Kench Tongue Lash: Lashes out to damage + slow (stuns at 3 passive stacks). Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Tahm Kench Tongue Lash: 7s at rank 1, and at three An Acquired Taste stacks it stuns instead of slowing. - Tahm Kench Abyssal Dive: 21s at rank 1 — his knockup engage and his only escape, so all-in inside it.

edits.before: His escape + shield. All-in when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 and it is his only escape — all-in inside it.

edits.before: That is Tahm Kench's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Tongue Lash only stuns at three An Acquired Taste stacks — count them before you walk up.

edits.before: Charging Q into a waiting Abyssal Dive — losing the stun before you land it means you took the whole trade for nothing and your W mark expires un-cashed.
edits.after: Thick Skin is a 3s cooldown that turns stored damage into a shield and heals him out of combat — buy Grievous Wounds instead of waiting it out.

edits.before: You out-brawl Kench in melee: E Sky Splitter slow into Q Thundering Smash stun interrupts his W Devour dive and pins him for W Frenzied Maul bleeds. Your Passive attack speed ramps faster than his Q Tongue Lash poke can trade, so short fights are yours.
edits.after: You out-brawl Kench in melee: Sky Splitter's slow into the Thundering Smash stun pins him, and Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1, so once he spends it he cannot leave. The Relentless Storm ramps faster than Tongue Lash's 7s poke can trade, so short fights are yours.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's utility outscales your lane: W Devour saves allies, R Abyssal Voyage sets up ganks and dives, and full-tank stacking soaks your combo. His grey-health passive and peel make him a fight-warper even after losing lane.
edits.after: Tahm Kench's utility outscales your lane: Devour (R) swallows an ally straight out of your all-in, Abyssal Dive knocks you up from 1000 range, and full-tank stacking soaks your combo. He warps fights even after losing the lane outright.

edits.before: The lane is yours start to finish, but two items in Tahm Kench tilts the game his way. W Devour peel, R Abyssal Voyage roams and dives, and full-tank stacking make him a fight-warping support-tank your solo-kill lead can't match. The 51.6% win rate reflects a lane you win that he offsets with team utility.
edits.after: The lane is yours start to finish, but two items in Tahm Kench tilts the game his way. Devour (R) pulls your target out of a won fight, Abyssal Dive knocks up from 1000 range every 21s, and full-tank stacking makes him a fight-warper your solo-kill lead can't match. The 51.6% win rate reflects that trade.

notes: 'Abyssal Voyage' is a champion-wide problem, not just this matchup — the mirror audit counted it in 26 places across nine tahmkench entries. It was removed in the 2020 rework; the current W is Abyssal Dive. Worth a global sweep outside this run. Devour was also written as his W in six fields here; it is his R.
